title: Gaṅgādhara Sadāśiva Praṇām-mantram
author: Sanskrit composition
by Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj

translation: The chief of the Demigods, whose body is decorated by snakes, whose body shines like the moon, who has five heads, who carries his weapon known as Paśupat, who gives boons, who is of satisfied nature, who holds the Gaṅgā on his head, who maintains those who give obeisances to him, who is easily pleased – I offer my obeisances to Sadāśiva who is dear to Hari, and whose crown is the moon.

head.description: Gaṅgādhara Sadāśiva Praṇām-mantram — a Vaiṣṇava song by Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj with lyrics, English translation and word-by-word meaning. From Kirtan Guide.
